issues.detail: The Greek 'υιος' (huios) is translated as 'Con' (capitalized/Son) in the first instance, but the Greek does not specify a capital letter or a specific title other than 'son'. More importantly, the Vietnamese 'nếu là Con' (if [I] am Son) introduces a conditional structure ('nếu... thì') that is not present in the Greek. The Greek 'αλλ υιος ει δε υιος' uses 'δε' as a coordinating conjunction (but/and also) to emphasize 'son' AND 'heir', not as a conditional 'if'. The Vietnamese makes it sound like 'if I am a son, then I am an heir,' whereas the Greek says 'I am a son and an heir'.
